And so, we believe that our policy will ultimately benefit not just  workers and firms and households in general, but will benefit savers as well, as the returns that  they can earn on their investments will improve with the improvement in the economy.
We believe that a good bit of the unemployment that we are seeing is what  economists would call cyclical unemployment—that is, unemployment arising because of  inadequate demand in the economy.

Now, it’s also possible that part of the increase in unemployment reflects so-called  structural factors—mismatches between worker skills and job opportunities, loss of skills,  geographical mismatch, et cetera.

And we’ll continue to ask ourselves whether or not additional stimulus  or additional actions can provide a better outcome, and that’s certainly something that remains  on the table and we’ll continue to evaluate as we go forward.
